Q1 2026: THB/USD Performance Summary
In the first quarter of 2026, the Thai Baht (THB) experienced a "Volatile U-Turn," shifting from early strength to a sharp decline due to external shocks.
1. "Trump 2.0" Tariffs
•
Early Surge: The Baht initially strengthened as Thai exporters "front-loaded" 
shipments to the US to beat impending tariffs, creating a temporary trade 
surplus.
•
Policy Impact: The implementation of a 10%–15% US global import 
surcharge eventually dampened investor confidence. This shift fueled a 
"risk-off" sentiment, driving capital back into the US Dollar as a safe-haven.
2. Middle East & Strait of Hormuz Crisis
• Energy Shock: The closure of the Strait of Hormuz caused global oil prices 
to skyrocket. As a net energy importer, Thailand’s current account was hit 
hard.
• Currency Weakening: High energy costs and geopolitical instability led to 
a massive sell-off of the Baht. By late March, the THB weakened 
significantly toward the 33.00 THB/USD range.
